mechanism: the upstream host is a destructuring default (`apiHost = 'https://api.minimax.io'`), so the pinned process runs with node-fetch replaced by a controlled peer (tools/lib/pinned-outbound.mjs); both the outbound request and the peer response are captured, and nothing is inferred

methods.URL construction: `${apiHost}/v1/t2a_v2` is plain concatenation: no trailing-slash normalisation, no encoding
methods.default semantics: the eight defaults are destructuring initializers, so they fire on undefined only; null and "" are used verbatim
methods.error taxonomy: non-ok upstream answers JSON-parse the body first and fall back to text; base_resp.status_code is compared strictly against the number 0; base_resp.status_msg is interpolated, so an absent one renders the literal "undefined"
methods.audio hex: the payload is hex-decoded after stripping a leading "0x" and every whitespace character; an odd length is LEFT-padded with a zero

conventions.mock: peer origins are recorded as the <mock> marker; the Go replay substitutes its own listener
conventions.closed: a transport failure is recorded as the <closed> marker; the Go replay binds and closes a real local port, so the failure is produced rather than simulated

nodeFetchWireDefaults.verifiedBy: tests/oracle/sillytavern-1.19.0-sd-routes.json records the same defaults on the pinned wire against a real local peer

shapeReason.voice.url.throws body: that branch interpolates the transport error message, which carries the request authority (node-fetch renders "request to <url> failed, reason: ECONNREFUSED <host>:<port>"); the value is a property of the transport, so no value is recorded and the 500 status plus the two outbound requests are compared instead
